answer.rationale: Competitive price-cut by rival directly targeting SMB base with doubled churn signals urgent need for retention response. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_31 confirms simplification also works for SMB activation, but pricing pressure is immediate and retention-focused. Promotional pricing addresses the direct competitive threat while memory_73 establishes it can drive qualified revenue in this exact segment. Standard experiment scope mitigates discount erosion risk while gathering fresh data on price elasticity under competitive duress. Risk flagged: sustained pricing discounting could compress margins and train price-sensitive customers toward deal-hunting behavior, potentially weakening LTV sustainability. Uncertainty preserved: competitive response timing and SMB segment elasticity under concurrent competitor pressure remain partially unknown; standard test allows measurement before broader rollout. Alternatives rejected: simplification/messaging are acquisition/engagement plays, not retention defenses; referral incentives and enterprise focus misaligned with immediate SMB churn crisis.
